question: Acetyl-CoA:

options.opa: It is synthesized from pyruvate in the eukaryotic cytoplasm.
options.opb: It has a phosphate bond rich in energy.
options.opc: Presents a guanine nucleotide in coenzyme A.
options.opd: Activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase.
options.ope: It easily crosses the mitochondrial inner membrane.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acetyl-CoA -> synthesized from pyruvate in the eukaryotic cytoplasm -> 50% CHAIN: Acetyl-CoA -> has a phosphate bond rich in energy -> 80% CHAIN: Acetyl-CoA -> presents a guanine nucleotide in coenzyme A -> 70% CHAIN: Acetyl-CoA -> activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase -> 60% CHAIN: Acetyl-CoA -> easily crosses the mitochondrial inner membrane -> 50%
analysis: Acetyl-CoA is synthesized from pyruvate in the mitochondrial matrix, not in the eukaryotic cytoplasm. It does not have a phosphate bond rich in energy, but rather contains a thioester bond. Coenzyme A in Acetyl-CoA does not contain a guanine nucleotide. Acetyl-CoA activates pyruvate dehydrogenase and inhibits pyruvate carboxylase. Acetyl-CoA cannot easily cross the mitochondrial inner membrane.
